- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; apply a 2–5% downward bias to correct for lagged mean reversion.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates the drop; add 1–2% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model tends to overcorrect after mean-reversion periods; if 3+ consecutive days show price moving toward historical mean, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price increases (especially after sentiment shifts upward); adjust forecast upward by 0.5–2% for final 5–7 days if sentiment rises.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.2–0.5 values), model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–2% noise in forecast to reflect sentiment-driven uncertainty.
